material_systems.name: Block Filler for CMU (PCA P12 Level 2 Standard Fill)

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry Block Filler
specialty.notes: Mandatory for CMU substrate — fills voids to PCA P12 Level 2 (max 10 voids per SF). Not a primer — substrate preparation product. Heavy-body material requiring 527-535 spray tip (0.025-0.035 orifice) and 30-mesh coarse filter. Pressure: 2,300-3,000 PSI. Backroll mandatory after spray to force filler into voids.

material_systems.notes: Block filler is applied BEFORE alkali-resistant primer. CMU without block filler will have voids that telegraph through primer and finish coats. Coverage is very low due to void filling — the most material-intensive step in masonry coating. QT level does not affect block filler application — always required on CMU.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Masonry & Stucco Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY on ALL new masonry regardless of quality tier — pH 12-14 requires alkali-resistant primer. Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable. SW Loxon is rated to pH 13, enabling 7-day accelerated coating (vs 28-day standard cure). Apply over block filler on CMU, directly to bare masonry on brick/concrete/limestone.

material_systems.notes: Non-negotiable primer for new masonry. The alkali-resistance is not quality-optional — even QT2 must use this primer. Coverage varies significantly by substrate texture: smooth face brick 300-350 SF/gal, rough/tumbled brick 200-275 SF/gal, primed CMU (over block filler) 275-350 SF/gal, cast concrete 250-325 SF/gal.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Masonry

finish.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior for masonry walls. 10-20 perms breathability preserves vapor diffusion. 6-8 mils DFT. QT2 allows single finish coat on properly primed surface. QT3 requires two coats standard. Preserves masonry texture, superior UV resistance vs elastomeric.

material_systems.notes: Primary finish system for residential masonry. Flat is budget standard. Satin is most common residential choice — hides surface irregularity while providing durability and cleanability. Coverage is lower than siding due to masonry porosity and texture.

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Finish for Masonry

finish.notes: Premium 100% acrylic for QT4 masonry. Superior color retention, fade resistance, and film build. Raking light inspection between coats on visible areas. Light sand (220 grit) between coats if surface anomalies detected. 10-20 perms breathability preserved.

material_systems.notes: Premium tier for high-end residential masonry. Same sheen options as standard — semi-gloss is not typical for masonry wall field (texture irregularities are magnified). Premium products provide better hide, fade resistance, and longevity.

material_systems.name: Elastomeric Coating for Masonry

products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec Elastomeric Waterproof Coating
finish.notes: Elastomeric coating: 20-30 mils DFT, 300-500% elongation, 5-15 perms. Bridges hairline cracks up to 1/16 inch. Two coats mandatory — single coat cannot achieve required DFT. Material cost is 3-4x that of standard acrylic due to extremely low coverage. Requires 527-535 spray tip and 30-mesh filter for airless application.

material_systems.notes: Elastomeric coatings are inherently flat/low-sheen due to film thickness. Not available at QT2 — application complexity exceeds economy scope. WARNING: High risk of catastrophic delamination if moisture enters from alternate sources (ground water, plumbing leaks, rising damp). Requires documented moisture source assessment before specification. Not recommended for below-grade or earth-contact surfaces.

CMU.notes: CMU block filler coverage varies widely by void density and block profile. Standard-weight CMU: ~100 SF/gal. Lightweight/open-texture CMU: as low as 75 SF/gal. Dense split-face CMU: up to 125 SF/gal.

assumptions: Coverage is for single coat block filler application with spray + backroll.
Spray application: transfer efficiency is low (~50-60%) due to heavy-body material — already factored into range.
Split-face CMU has deeper voids requiring significantly more material per SF.

brick_smooth.notes: Smooth face brick — relatively dense, low porosity. Best primer coverage of masonry types.

brick_rough.notes: Rough/tumbled/antique face brick — deep mortar joints, irregular surface. Significantly more material consumed.

CMU_filled.notes: CMU after block filler application — surface is sealed by filler, improving primer coverage. Comparable to smooth brick.

concrete.notes: Cast concrete — variable porosity depending on form quality and finishing. Bug holes and form marks reduce coverage.

limestone.notes: Limestone — highly porous sedimentary stone. Lower coverage due to absorption. Ensure high-perm primer (>10 perms).

assumptions: Coverage rates are for brush/roll application. Spray_backroll adds 25% material for transfer efficiency loss.
Mortar joint depth affects coverage — deep-raked joints consume more material than flush-tooled joints.
CMU coverage assumes block filler has been applied. Unfiltered CMU primer coverage would be much lower.

brick_smooth.notes: Smooth face brick on primed surface. Primer seals porosity — finish coat coverage is consistent.

brick_rough.notes: Rough/tumbled brick — mortar joints and texture consume more material even on primed surface.

CMU_filled_primed.notes: CMU after block filler + primer. Surface is well-sealed — good finish coat coverage.

concrete.notes: Cast concrete on primed surface. Bug holes may still show through — coverage moderate.

limestone.notes: Limestone on primed surface. Porous substrate may still draw material through primer seal.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two-coat system at QT3/QT4 doubles material consumption.
Spray_backroll application: multiply material quantity by 1.25 for transfer efficiency loss.
Premium acrylic (QT4) slightly lower coverage due to higher solids content — reflected in base rate.

brick_smooth.notes: Elastomeric on smooth brick — dramatically lower coverage due to 20-30 mil DFT. 3-4x material vs acrylic.

brick_rough.notes: Elastomeric on rough brick — texture amplifies already-low coverage. Most material-intensive combination.

CMU_filled_primed.notes: Elastomeric on filled/primed CMU. Block filler smooths surface somewhat but thick-film DFT dominates.

concrete.notes: Elastomeric on primed concrete. Bug holes and form marks still consume extra material.

limestone.notes: Elastomeric on limestone — highest material consumption. Question breathability at 5-15 perms on porous limestone.

assumptions: Coverage per coat. Two coats mandatory — single coat cannot achieve 20-30 mil DFT target.
Spray_backroll is the only practical method for elastomeric (too thick for roller-only at production scale).
Transfer efficiency for elastomeric spray is lower than acrylic (~50%) due to heavy-body material.
Material cost: elastomeric is approximately $50-80/gal vs $35-55/gal for premium acrylic. Combined with 3-4x lower coverage, material cost per SF is 5-8x higher than acrylic.

consumables.name: Roller cover 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap (masonry)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 150 SF rolled (heavy texture shreds nap faster than smooth surfaces)
consumables.notes: Heavy nap roller for porous/rough masonry surfaces. Nylon/polyester blend for water-based products. Much thicker nap than interior (3/8) or siding (3/4) rollers. Required for backroll step and roll-only applications.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 517 (masonry acrylic/primer)
consumables.notes: 0.017 orifice for standard acrylic latex and alkali-resistant primer on masonry. Also 619, 621 for wider patterns on large wall fields. Cementitious substrate causes faster tip wear than wood — shorter service life per tip.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 531 (block filler / elastomeric)
consumables.notes: 0.025-0.035 orifice (527, 531, 535 range) for heavy-body block fillers and elastomeric coatings. Requires 2,300-3,000 PSI. Faster wear rate due to abrasive heavy-body material.

consumables.name: 60-mesh spray filter (black) for latex
consumables.notes: Standard 60-mesh (black/medium) filter for acrylic latex exterior coatings and alkali-resistant primer. Change when flow rate drops.

consumables.name: 30-mesh spray filter (gray/coarse) for block filler and elastomeric
consumables.notes: Coarse 30-mesh (gray) filter for block fillers and elastomeric coatings. Heavy-body materials clog standard 60-mesh filters. Essential for preventing tip blockage and maintaining consistent flow.

consumables.name: Red stucco poly tape (7.0 mil, 30-day UV)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 ROLL (60 yd) per 50 LF of masking lines
consumables.notes: Masking tape specifically for rough masonry/stucco surfaces. Standard blue painter's tape will NOT adhere to textured masonry — it lacks the adhesive strength and conformability for rough profiles. 7.0 mil thickness, 30-day UV rating for multi-day exterior projects. Red stucco tape is the ONLY acceptable masking tape for masonry.

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting for exterior protection (4 mil UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: 4 mil minimum thickness. UV-resistant for multi-day exterior projects. Used for landscape perimeter, hardscape, HVAC unit, and light fixture overspray protection. Heavier than interior plastic — must withstand wind and weather.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.notes: Heavy canvas drop cloths for hardscape walkway and patio protection. Non-slip surface for crew traffic. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Painter's tape (exterior grade, UV-resistant)
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape. 14-day removal rating minimum. Used for light fixture and HVAC unit masking where surfaces are smooth (not masonry). For masking ON masonry surfaces, use CON_MSRY_STUCCO_TAPE instead. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Polyurethane exterior caulk (Class 25/50)
consumables.usage_rate: 1 TUBE per 25 LF of masonry-to-trim joints
consumables.notes: Polyurethane caulk for masonry-to-trim joints, masonry-to-window/door frame joints. Class 25 minimum (25% joint movement tolerance). 3-7 day cure before painting. Siliconized acrylic acceptable for low-movement joints. Do NOT use silicone — not paintable.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) cleaner
consumables.notes: For masonry washing at QT3/QT4 (moderate efflorescence, general cleaning). TSP solution applied with stiff brush, rinsed thoroughly. Do NOT mix TSP with acids. At QT2, water wash may substitute.

consumables.name: Stiff bristle masonry brush
consumables.usage_rate: 1 EA per 1000 SF scrubbed (replace when bristles flatten)
consumables.notes: Heavy-duty stiff bristle brush for efflorescence removal, masonry scrubbing, and general prep. Poly or tampico bristle — not wire (wire can embed in mortar joints and rust).

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.notes: For intercoat sanding at QT4 only. Light scuff between finish coats when surface anomalies detected during raking light inspection. Reused consumable ID.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.notes: For dust removal after sanding before subsequent coat. QT4 interstage use only. Reused consumable ID.

ext_landscape_perimeter.description: House perimeter where landscape is adjacent — measured in LF along foundation/masonry wall line
ext_landscape_perimeter.notes: LF-based. Lay tarps along the perimeter where landscape beds, shrubs, and plants are adjacent to masonry wall. Spray_backroll: full tarp width over plantings (10-15 ft overspray drift). Roll: narrower coverage at base.

ext_hardscape_walk.description: Adjacent walkways requiring protection from overspray and drips
ext_hardscape_walk.notes: Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic. Plastic sheeting for spray overspray on areas without foot traffic.

ext_hardscape_patio.notes: Protection level driven by proximity and application method. Spray_backroll requires wider coverage than roll-only.

ext_light_fixture.description: Exterior light fixtures on or adjacent to masonry wall
ext_light_fixture.notes: Bag or tape over fixture with plastic. Remove fixture cover plate if accessible. Use blue tape on fixture surfaces (smooth) — stucco tape not needed on non-masonry surfaces.

ext_hvac_unit.description: HVAC condenser units adjacent to masonry wall
ext_hvac_unit.notes: Full tarp cover during spray operations. Do not block intake/exhaust if unit is running. Secure with weights or tape — wind can dislodge loose plastic.

compatibility_rules.description: Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED on alkaline masonry
compatibility_rules.notes: Alkaline hydroxides (pH 12-14) react with alkyd/oil paint esters through saponification — hydrolyzing binder into soft, sticky, water-soluble soap. Complete removal to bare masonry is the only remedy. Per Exterior_Primer_Systems_Doctrine.md §1: alkyd is 'Not Recommended For' brick, concrete, stucco.

compatibility_rules.description: Alkali-resistant primer mandatory on ALL new masonry
compatibility_rules.notes: New masonry pH 12-14 requires alkali-resistant primer regardless of quality tier. Standard acrylic primer (designed for pH <9) will suffer alkali burn — pigment attack, binder degradation, total coating failure. Even QT2 economy must use alkali-resistant primer.

compatibility_rules.description: Block filler mandatory for CMU substrate before primer
compatibility_rules.notes: CMU voids telegraph through primer and finish if not filled. Block filler (PCA P12 Level 2) is substrate preparation, not primer. Applied BEFORE alkali-resistant primer. Required at all quality tiers including QT2.

compatibility_rules.description: Elastomeric coating requires moisture source assessment
compatibility_rules.required_action: Document moisture source assessment before specification
compatibility_rules.notes: Elastomeric coatings (5-15 perms) are less breathable than standard acrylic (10-20 perms). If moisture enters from alternate sources (ground water, plumbing leaks, rising damp), it becomes trapped behind the elastomeric film, causing catastrophic delamination. The painter must verify no alternate moisture sources exist.
Elastomeric application complexity (thick-film DFT control, heavy-body spray, extended dry times) exceeds economy scope. Per resolution: elastomeric is QT3/QT4 only.

compatibility_rules.description: No acid cleaning on limestone substrate
compatibility_rules.notes: Limestone is calcite-based sedimentary stone. Acid dissolves calcite, causing irreversible surface damage, pitting, and structural weakening. Efflorescence on limestone must be treated with water + stiff brush only, or specialty non-acidic masonry cleaners.

compatibility_rules.description: Moisture content must be below 12% before coating
compatibility_rules.required_action: Moisture test per ASTM D4263 or equivalent. MC > 12% = HARD STOP
compatibility_rules.notes: Coating over wet masonry (MC >12%) causes blistering, delamination, and premature failure. All product systems require dry substrate. This is a pre-application verification, not a material selection rule.

compatibility_rules.description: Spray on masonry requires backroll — no spray-only
compatibility_rules.required_action: Convert to spray_backroll — spray-only is PROHIBITED on porous masonry
compatibility_rules.notes: Spray bridges over pinholes/voids in porous masonry. Backroll forces coating into pores for continuous film and proper DFT. Per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine Part A §6: spray on masonry = auto-add backroll.

risk_notes.risk: Oil-based or alkyd paints on alkaline masonry (pH 12-14) undergo saponification — alkaline hydroxides hydrolyze paint esters into soft, sticky, water-soluble soap. Complete removal to bare masonry is the only remedy.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use ONLY water-based acrylic or elastomeric products. Alkali-resistant primer (SYS_EXT_MSRY_PRIMER_ALKALI) as first coat. Never substitute standard primer.

risk_notes.risk: Elastomeric coatings (5-15 perms) are less breathable than acrylic (10-20 perms). If moisture enters from alternate sources (rising damp, plumbing leaks, grade contact), it becomes trapped behind the thick elastomeric film. Hydrostatic pressure builds and catastrophically delaminates the entire coating system in large sheets.
risk_notes.mitigation: Require documented moisture source assessment before elastomeric specification. Verify no below-grade moisture, no plumbing in wall cavity, no rising damp. If uncertain, specify acrylic instead.

risk_notes.topic: Spalling from moisture entrapment in freeze-thaw climates
risk_notes.risk: Non-breathable coatings trap moisture behind film. In freeze-thaw climates, trapped water expands ~9%, shearing off the outer face of masonry units (spalling). Spalling is irreversible substrate damage — exposes soft interior to rapid structural deterioration.
risk_notes.mitigation: Ensure coating system breathability is adequate for substrate porosity. High-perm acrylic (10-20 perms) is safer than elastomeric (5-15 perms) in freeze-thaw climates. For limestone and historic brick, breathability is paramount.

risk_notes.risk: Elastomeric coating is 3-4x the per-gallon cost of standard acrylic AND achieves 3-4x lower coverage (50-150 SF/gal vs 200-350 SF/gal). Combined effect: material cost per SF is 5-8x higher than standard acrylic. A 2000 SF masonry wall with elastomeric may consume 30-40 gallons vs 8-12 gallons for acrylic.
risk_notes.mitigation: Flag material cost escalation to customer at specification time. Ensure elastomeric is justified by crack-bridging need — do not default to elastomeric when acrylic is sufficient.

risk_notes.topic: Spray overspray drift on masonry projects
risk_notes.risk: Airless spray overspray drifts 10-15 ft. Masonry projects often involve large wall areas generating significant overspray volume. Adjacent landscaping, vehicles, hardscape, and neighboring structures at risk.
risk_notes.mitigation: Full landscape/hardscape protection for spray_backroll applications. Wind monitoring — stop spray if wind exceeds 10 mph. Roll-only method eliminates overspray risk for occupied-adjacent scenarios.

risk_notes.risk: Efflorescence (white salt deposits) on new masonry indicates internal moisture migration. Coating over active efflorescence leads to salt deposit buildup behind paint film, causing blistering and delamination. Efflorescence is a symptom — coating cannot solve the moisture source.
risk_notes.mitigation: Treat efflorescence per cleaning hierarchy. Verify and correct moisture source before coating. Document efflorescence presence and treatment in project file. If efflorescence recurs during cure period, escalate to structural assessment.

risk_notes.topic: Block filler tip wear and equipment demands
risk_notes.risk: Block filler and elastomeric coatings are heavy-body materials that cause accelerated spray tip wear (0.025-0.035 tips) and require higher PSI (2,300-3,000). Standard residential sprayers may not deliver adequate pressure for large-area CMU or elastomeric work.
risk_notes.mitigation: Verify sprayer capacity before mobilization. Budget for additional spray tips (higher wear rate). Use 30-mesh coarse filters instead of standard 60-mesh.

material_quantity_notes.spray_transfer_efficiency: Airless spray on masonry: 50-70% transfer efficiency depending on surface roughness and wind. Multiply theoretical coverage by 1.25-1.50 for overspray, misting, and pattern overlap. Elastomeric/block filler spray: closer to 50% transfer due to heavy-body material.
material_quantity_notes.surface_texture_factor: Smooth face brick: 1.00x. Rough/tumbled brick: 1.30x. Split-face CMU: 1.50x. Applied on top of substrate-specific coverage rate. Texture modifier affects ALL product layers (filler, primer, finish).
material_quantity_notes.coat_count_standard: Block filler: 1 coat (CMU only). Alkali-resistant primer: 1 coat (all substrates). Finish acrylic: QT2=1 coat, QT3/QT4=2 coats. Finish elastomeric: 2 coats mandatory (DFT target requires it).
material_quantity_notes.mortar_joint_depth: Deep-raked mortar joints (>3/8 inch recess) increase material consumption by 10-15% over flush-tooled joints. Not captured in surface_texture_modifier — treat as separate adjustment if known.
material_quantity_notes.cmu_total_material_stack: CMU at QT3 acrylic requires: 1 coat block filler (100 SF/gal) + 1 coat primer (300 SF/gal) + 2 coats finish (300 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF CMU wall: ~10 gal filler + ~3.3 gal primer + ~6.6 gal finish = ~20 gal total. Spray waste adds 25-50%.
material_quantity_notes.elastomeric_total_material: Elastomeric at QT3 on brick: 1 coat primer (275 SF/gal) + 2 coats elastomeric (100 SF/gal each). For 1000 SF brick wall: ~3.6 gal primer + ~20 gal elastomeric = ~24 gal total. Spray waste adds 30-50%.

assumptions.note: Coverage varies by void density and CMU block profile. Conservative midpoint (100 SF/gal) used for estimation.

Doctrine states 250-350 SF/gal for porous substrates. Extended to 200 SF/gal lower bound for rough/tumbled brick and limestone based on field experience. Doctrine confirms primer coverage is porosity-dependent.

Doctrine states 'significantly lower coverage due to 20-30 mil DFT' but does not specify exact SF/gal. Derived from DFT requirement and manufacturer PDS data. 100 SF/gal midpoint on smooth substrate, 75 SF/gal on textured. Flag for field calibration.

assumptions.value: Red stucco poly tape required instead of standard blue tape for masking ON masonry surfaces
assumptions.note: Exterior_Protection_Doctrine does not specifically address tape selection for rough masonry surfaces. Field experience confirms standard blue tape does not adhere to textured masonry. Stucco tape is the field-standard solution.

assumptions.value: Acrylic coatings (10-20 perms) acceptable; elastomeric (5-15 perms) marginal on highly porous limestone
assumptions.note: Doctrine identifies limestone as requiring breathable coatings and mineral silicate (77+ perms) as ideal. Standard acrylic at 10-20 perms is a practical compromise for residential scope. Elastomeric on limestone is flagged as risk — breathability may be insufficient in freeze-thaw climates.

uncertainty_flags.description: Exact SF/gal for elastomeric on various masonry substrates is not established in doctrine. Manufacturer PDS data varies significantly (50-200 SF/gal). DFT-based calculation suggests 75-125 SF/gal for 20-30 mil target. Field calibration needed.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Material quantity estimates for elastomeric jobs may be off by 25-50%. Budget conservatively.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field calibration data from 3-5 elastomeric masonry projects.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Mortar joint depth impact on coverage
uncertainty_flags.description: Deep-raked mortar joints (common on some architectural brick) increase material consumption significantly, but the magnitude is not well-quantified in doctrine (estimated 10-15%).
uncertainty_flags.impact: Brick walls with deep-raked joints may consume 10-15% more material than predicted by surface_texture_modifier alone.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Mortar joint depth as optional PaintScope input, or add mortar_profile modifier to coverage_profiles.

uncertainty_flags.topic: Spray transfer efficiency on rough masonry
uncertainty_flags.description: Transfer efficiency for airless spray on rough masonry is estimated at 50-70% but varies with surface roughness, wind conditions, and operator technique. Elastomeric spray may be even lower due to material viscosity.
uncertainty_flags.impact: Material waste could be higher than modeled for rough substrates or windy conditions.
uncertainty_flags.resolution_needed: Field measurement of actual material consumption vs theoretical coverage on masonry substrates.
